# Naim Montazeri, Ph.D.

## Microbial Food Safety \| Predictive Modeling \| Risk Assessment

I am an Assistant Professor at the University of Florida with over 15 years of experience in microbial food safety, risk assessment, and predictive modeling. My work integrates experimental microbiology with R-based data analysis to evaluate pathogen persistence, transfer, and control in foods and agricultural systems, with particular experience in high-risk ready-to-eat foods, agricultural water, and risk-based strategies that support food safety decision-making and regulatory compliance. I also have experience applying FDA BAM, ISO, ASTM, AOAC, and EPA-aligned methods in food safety, sanitation, and validation studies.

My work is cross-functional, combining microbiology, data analysis, applied food safety, stakeholder outreach, science communication, and mentoring. Prior to my current role, I worked on sanitation validation, product development, processing, and quality evaluation in laboratory and pilot-scale environments, including antimicrobial interventions, thermal processing, sensory quality, and product stability.
:::

## Experience Snapshot

-   Assistant Professor, University of Florida — Microbial Food Safety (2018–present)
-   Postdoctoral Researcher, North Carolina State University — Food Virology (2015–2018)
-   Research Assistant, Louisiana State University — Food and Environmental Microbiology (2012–2015)
-   Research Assistant, University of Alaska Fairbanks — Food Safety and Quality (2009–2011)
-   Food Quality Assurance Intern, Pasargad Laboratory (2008–2009)

## Selected Focus Areas

-   Sanitation validation and environmental monitoring
-   Predictive microbiology and R-based modeling
-   Agricultural water and FSMA compliance
-   Thermal processing and pathogen inactivation
-   Product development and quality/sensory attributes
